entries.claim: A real teacher wrote the text-to-SQL training data
entries.evidence: Nemotron 3 Ultra on Nebius Token Factory wrote the databases, questions and SQL. Every SQL query ran in a sandbox and was kept only if it ran and returned rows. 821 training rows; 172 exam rows from held-out database domains.

check.label: Read the generator: a query is kept only if it runs and returns rows

entries.claim: A LoRA adapter was trained on that data
entries.evidence: Trained on a free Google Colab T4 GPU, not on Nebius GPUs: a 4-bit LoRA (r=16) on Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, 206 steps over 2 epochs in 66 minutes. Training loss went from 0.334 to 0.075; a training loss is not a quality result.

check.label: Read the training script that ran on the T4

entries.claim: How well the adapter does on the held-out exam
entries.evidence: The base model and the adapter each answered all 172 held-out exam rows; an answer is right when running it returns the same rows as the stored reference query on the same database. Strict (one reference per question): adapter 57 of 172, base 22 of 172, and the teacher answering the same prompts 44 of 172. Every number is recomputed from the raw answers by one script. The adapter is about three times better than the base and in the same range as the teacher; it does not yet replace the teacher at a 95 percent precision target.

check.label: Recompute the numbers from the raw answers (the answers are in evidence/text2sql-round1 once it is merged)
check.command: python scripts/measure_adapter.py verify --raw raw.jsonl --results results.json --golden golden.jsonl --dbs dbs.json

facts.label: Exam rows

metrics.label: Coverage (answered by the adapter)
